deck.audience: ML researchers, AI security practitioners, and cloud infrastructure engineers evaluating LLM API integrity

brief.title: Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs: Why Software Tests Fail and Hardware Attestation Wins
brief.one_liner: Commercial LLM API providers may covertly substitute cheaper models; this work shows software-based detection is unreliable and proposes TEEs as a provably secure alternative.
brief.goal: Understand the model substitution threat in LLM APIs, see empirical evidence that statistical and log-probability detection methods fail under realistic conditions, and recognize Trusted Execution Environments as the actionable path to verifiable inference.

slides.title: Are You Getting What You Pay For? Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs
slides.objective: Cover slide with paper title (referencing arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715) and a concise tagline about the trust gap in commercial LLM APIs.

slides.title: The Model Substitution Problem: Economic Incentives Drive Covert Swaps
slides.objective: Explain the core problem: providers may replace advertised models with quantized, smaller, or different models to cut costs. Show the four substitution types (smaller model, quantized variant, fine-tuned version, different family) in a structured diagram or list. Reference the formal hypothesis testing framework (H0 vs H1).

slides.title: FP8 Quantization Preserves Most Accuracy — Making Substitution Hard to Detect
slides.objective: Present the table comparing original vs FP8-quantized model scores across MMLU, GSM8K, MATH, and GPQA Diamond for five model families. Highlight that performance drops are small (often within error bars), motivating why detection is difficult. Use the benchmark data table.

slides.title: Higher Temperature Amplifies Performance Gaps but Increases Noise
slides.objective: Show the four-panel chart (figure_1.jpg) of benchmark accuracy vs temperature for all five models. Explain that at temperature 2.0 performance degrades across the board, and the gap between original and substitute narrows or becomes noisy, complicating statistical detection.

slides.title: Log Probability Fingerprinting Fails Due to Inference Nondeterminism
slides.objective: Display the log-probability scatter plot (figure_5.jpg) showing that the same Llama-3-8B model produces varying log probabilities across different software versions (transformers, vLLM) and hardware (A100, H100). Explain that this production-level nondeterminism defeats metadata-based detection methods.

slides.title: Randomized Routing at Low Rates Makes Statistical Detection Query-Prohibitive
slides.objective: Explain the randomized substitution attack where the provider mixes substitute responses with probability p. Show that as p approaches 0, the mixed distribution converges to the specified model's distribution, requiring exponentially more queries for detection. Use a conceptual diagram or formula visualization.

slides.title: Software-Only Auditing Methods Are Fundamentally Unreliable
slides.objective: Summarize the three failure modes: (1) text-based statistical tests (e.g., MMD) need too many queries and fail against subtle substitutions, (2) log-probability methods are defeated by nondeterminism, (3) adversarial countermeasures like benchmark evasion and randomized routing further undermine detection. Present as a structured comparison or matrix.

slides.title: Trusted Execution Environments Provide Provable Cryptographic Model Integrity
slides.objective: Introduce TEEs as the proposed solution. Explain how hardware-level attestation guarantees that the correct model weights are loaded and executed, with only modest performance overhead. Contrast TEE properties (provable, efficient, robust) against software methods. Mention NVIDIA confidential computing as a practical deployment path.

slides.title: Key Takeaways: Close the Verification Gap with Hardware Attestation
slides.objective: Summarize 4-5 key findings: (1) model substitution is economically motivated and practically undetectable via software, (2) FP8 quantization barely affects benchmarks, (3) inference nondeterminism kills log-prob fingerprinting, (4) randomized substitution defeats statistical tests, (5) TEEs are the only currently viable path to verifiable LLM APIs. End with a call to action for the community.
